about.description:
Package containing all the necessary CUDA driver files related to forward
compatibility, for the Jetson Orin family. This compatibility enables newer
CUDA runtimes to work with the older display driver shipped by JetPack 6 / L4T.
The data center and desktop GPUs are covered by `cuda-compat` instead.

The libraries are installed in `$PREFIX/cuda-compat`, which is not on the loader path.
They are picked up only if that directory is prepended to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
about.summary: CUDA Compatibility Platform for Jetson Orin

name: cuda-compat-orin-split
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set name = "cuda-compat-orin" %}

# To update this recipe, bump the two values below and refresh the sha256 from
# https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/redist/redistrib_<cuda release>.json
#
#   version              "cuda_compat_orin".version in the manifest. It is the version of the
#                        redistributable, prefixed by the CUDA release it belongs to, which is
#                        why it doubles as the package version: "cuda-compat-orin 13.3.*" still
#                        selects the CUDA 13.3 shim. Keeping it in package/version and in the
#                        source url is also what lets the autotick bot bump this recipe.
#   driver_version       the user-mode driver shipped by "cuda_compat_orin", which the
#                        manifest does not report: it is the suffix of the library file names
#                        inside the archive, e.g. compat_orin/libnvidia-nvvm.so.610.01.
#                        A stale value cannot slip through: the package tests below assert that
#                        every versioned library the archive ships carries this exact suffix.
{% set version = "13.3.45405995" %}
{% set driver_version = "610.01" %}
{% set cuda_version = version.split('.')[:2] | join('') %}

# Tegra cannot reuse the SBSA archive: its libcuda is built against the L4T kernel driver and
# links against the Tegra NVRM stack (libnvrm_gpu, libnvrm_mem, ...), absent on server ARM.
# NVIDIA therefore ships the separate "cuda_compat_orin" redistributable, the only supported
# way to run a CUDA 13 runtime on a Jetson Orin still on JetPack 6. Since CUDA 13 unified the
# Tegra and SBSA toolkits, it is published under the "linux-sbsa" platform directory, but it
# keeps its own layout: it is versioned after the CUDA release instead of the driver, and it
# unpacks into "compat_orin" instead of "compat".

package:
  name: {{ name|lower }}-split
  version: {{ version }}

source:
  url: https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/redist/cuda_compat_orin/linux-sbsa/cuda_compat_orin-linux-sbsa-{{ version }}-archive.tar.xz
  sha256: d9e7655f46c10eeda7c3652f4fce91825f2b446fab8976c4591bfd4b887e4c8d

build:
  number: 0
  skip: true  # [not aarch64]
  script:
    # An unmatched glob would otherwise reach check-glibc as a literal, which skips arguments
    # that are not files and still exits 0.
    - shopt -s failglob
    # check-glibc stays here, and not in the package tests, so that nothing is published if a
    # library needs a newer glibc than c_stdlib_version: a test can be skipped with --no-test,
    # the build script cannot.
    - check-glibc compat_orin/*.so*
    - mkdir -p "${PREFIX}/cuda-compat"
    - cp -vd compat_orin/*.so* "${PREFIX}/cuda-compat/"

requirements:
  build:
    - cf-nvidia-tools 1.*  # [linux]

# Two outputs because a package has one version but there are two numbers worth selecting on:
# the metapackage carries the CUDA release, so that "cuda-compat-orin 13.3.*" asks for the shim
# of a given toolkit, while the output holding the files carries the user-mode driver version.
outputs:
  - name: cuda-compat-orin
    requirements:
      run:
        - {{ pin_subpackage("cuda-compat-orin-impl", exact=True) }}
    test:
      commands:
        # The metapackage ships no files, so this only checks that installing it does pull in the
        # shim. Without a test section conda-build would not even create the test environment,
        # and the exact pin above would never be solved.
        - test -L $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libcuda.so.1
    about:
      home: https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-toolkit
      license_file: LICENSE
      license: LicenseRef-NVIDIA-End-User-License-Agreement
      license_url: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/index.html
      summary: CUDA Compatibility Platform for Jetson Orin
      description: |
        Package containing all the necessary CUDA driver files related to forward
        compatibility, for the Jetson Orin family. This compatibility enables newer
        CUDA runtimes to work with the older display driver shipped by JetPack 6 / L4T.
        The data center and desktop GPUs are covered by `cuda-compat` instead.

        The libraries are installed in `$PREFIX/cuda-compat`, which is not on the loader path.
        They are picked up only if that directory is prepended to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
      doc_url: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/index.html

  - name: cuda-compat-orin-impl
    version: "{{ driver_version }}"
    files:
      - cuda-compat
    build:
      # The compiler run exports would otherwise pin the package to the gcc used to build it,
      # libgcc >=14 and libstdcxx >=14, which says nothing about these prebuilt binaries: not
      # one of them lists libgcc_s or libstdc++ among its DT_NEEDED entries.
      ignore_run_exports:
        - libgcc
        - libstdcxx
      # libcuda lives in the off-path $PREFIX/cuda-compat directory, so the libraries that
      # link against it cannot resolve it at build time.
      # The rest is the L4T NVRM stack and the DLA runtime, which ship with the JetPack BSP
      # and are resolved on the device by the system loader configuration.
      missing_dso_allowlist:
        - '*/libcuda.so*'
        - '*/libnvcuextend.so'
        - '*/libnvdla_runtime.so'
        - '*/libnvrm_gpu.so'
        - '*/libnvrm_host1x.so'
        - '*/libnvrm_mem.so'
        - '*/libnvrm_sync.so'
    requirements:
      build:
        # Nothing is compiled here. The C compiler is still pulled in because its activation
        # sets CONDA_BUILD_SYSROOT, which conda-build's overlinking check needs, and stdlib("c")
        # is what turns the c_stdlib_version pin into the __glibc >=2.28 run export.
        - {{ compiler("c") }}
        - {{ stdlib("c") }}
      run:
        # Orin moved to the sbsa ABI in CTK 13, so the arm-variant must always be sbsa here.
        # Requesting the tegra variant would make the package unsolvable together with the
        # rest of the CUDA 13 stack, which is sbsa only on aarch64.
        - arm-variant * sbsa
      run_constrained:
        # Orin is sm_87 and no discrete GPU shares that compute capability, so this bound just
        # states that the package targets a Jetson Orin. It is advisory: "__cuda_arch" comes
        # from CEP-46, pixi and rattler report it natively while conda needs the
        # "nvidia-virtual-packages" plugin, and a run_constrained on a missing virtual package
        # is vacuously satisfied.
        #
        # A hard run requirement would be stronger, but it cannot be used here: the build image
        # has no "__cuda_arch", so the test environment of this output becomes unsolvable and
        # the build fails with "nothing provides __cuda_arch 8.7.*". That no longer matters
        # much, since the package name is what keeps this shim away from sbsa users.
        - __cuda_arch 8.7.*
        # Both shims install into $PREFIX/cuda-compat, so co-installing them would clobber
        # files. They target disjoint hardware anyway, so make it a solver error.
        - cuda-compat-impl <0a0
    test:
      commands:
        # The Tegra libcuda keeps the L4T SONAME libcuda.so.1.1 instead of being versioned
        # after the driver, and libcudadebugger.so.1 is a regular file rather than a symlink.
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libcuda.so.1.1
        - test -L $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libcuda.so.1
        - test -L $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libcuda.so
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-nvvm.so.{{ driver_version }}
        - test -L $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-nvvm.so.4
        - test -L $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-nvvm.so
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-ptxjitcompiler.so.{{ driver_version }}
        - test -L $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-ptxjitcompiler.so.1
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-tileiras.so.{{ driver_version }}
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-gpucomp.so.{{ driver_version }}
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvidia-nvvm70.so.4
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libcudadebugger.so.1
        # Only Tegra ships the cuDLA bridge and the NVRM interop shim.
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvcudla.so
        - test -f $PREFIX/cuda-compat/libnvcuextend.so
    about:
      home: https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-toolkit
      license_file: LICENSE
      license: LicenseRef-NVIDIA-End-User-License-Agreement
      license_url: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/index.html
      summary: CUDA Compatibility Platform for Jetson Orin
      description: |
        Package containing all the necessary CUDA driver files related to forward
        compatibility, for the Jetson Orin family. This compatibility enables newer
        CUDA runtimes to work with the older display driver shipped by JetPack 6 / L4T.
        The data center and desktop GPUs are covered by `cuda-compat` instead.

        The libraries are installed in `$PREFIX/cuda-compat`, which is not on the loader path.
        They are picked up only if that directory is prepended to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
      doc_url: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/index.html
